I will use an instrumental variables (IV) approach to estimate the causal effect of military service on 1981 earnings. The treatment is `servic_indi_016`, and the outcome is the 1981 annual earnings (documented as the study's outcome, though the codebook suggests earnings are spread across several `earnin_` variables). I will use `low_number` as the instrument, as it was randomly assigned and significantly increased the probability of service. Alternatively, `station_delay` could serve as a source of exogenous variation for those whose files were lost in the 1970 fire. The main threat to the validity of `low_number` is the "veterans' preference" points given to anyone on the eligibility roll, which could affect earnings independently of actual service. This creates a violation of the exclusion restriction because the instrument (lottery number) affects the outcome (earnings) through a path other than the treatment (service).
